steps.what: Clarify the customer's routes, travel date and information need
Look up routes, gates, prices and timetable details
Explain the information and resolve uncertainty or accessibility questions

tasks.design: Configure a structured query in {OTHER}, the passenger information system, showing current source and update time. The attendant retains clarification, explanation and manual escalation when current data is unavailable.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts are found across separate timetable, fare and terminal screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing structured lookup can return a joined view without generated travel claims.
tasks.still_hard: Disruptions, ambiguous journeys and individual accessibility needs.
tasks.human_edge: Ensure the customer understands what the information means for the journey.
tasks.altitude: Less screen searching; customer assistance remains with the attendant.

evidence.claim: A deterministic lookup over current timetable and fare data is a model-knowledge design; no measured passenger-service case is supplied.

assumptions: Boundary is staff-assisted information, excluding booking changes, ticket sales and actual customer travel.
The attendant captures origin, destination, travel date, service identifier if known and requested information in s1; capture time remains. Unclear requests are resolved manually.

Transport control and fare administration produce route, service date, gate or terminal, timetable, fare conditions, disruption status and update timestamp before lookup; additional capture and freshness maintenance is counted as other-role upkeep. Missing or stale fields trigger manual checking with control, not a guessed answer.
Test native passenger-system views before custom integration. No unattended customer chatbot or automatic rerouting is proposed.
unknowns: Available source interfaces and update latency
Current lookup time and manual fallback load
research_questions: Does one source-linked view reduce total assistance time during disruptions?

already_counted.description: Query capture, explanation and manual uncertainty resolution

incremental.description: Service and fare capture, mapping and freshness maintenance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R70 gross30 minus8 upkeep gives net22. Range0-6 allows existing joined views or frequent stale service data to absorb most gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Verify tickets and record passenger movements

steps.what: Verify tickets and seat reservations and capture actual boarding or disembarking
Count movement entries and prepare passenger totals
Resolve count discrepancies and accept the passenger movement record

tasks.design: Configure movement capture and totals in {OTHER}, the passenger handling system. Retain actual ticket checks, entry capture, discrepancy resolution and acceptance; a reservation is never counted as actual boarding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual tallying and retranscription separate observations from totals.
tasks.enabler_now: Native entry lists and counters can aggregate verified movements.
tasks.still_hard: Duplicate scans, groups, missed exits and offline capture.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve who actually travelled rather than trusting a booking total.
tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic and transcription; physical checking remains.

evidence.claim: Deterministic counters can aggregate captured movement records; proposed shares and savings are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is attendant verification and counting, excluding booking administration and passenger movement time.

The attendant produces service identifier, stop, ticket or group identifier, direction, observed count, timestamp and exception note in s1, whose full 60 percent includes scanning or manual entry. Booking staff produce reservation data through unchanged existing work; no booking is treated as a movement.
Native counters run only on captured entries. Missing or offline entries use a manual tally later reconciled in s3; no inferred passenger flag is assumed.
Test native passenger-system capture and counters first; existing automated tally runtime earns no new saving.
unknowns: Existing scanning coverage and offline procedure
research_questions: Does total time fall after including movement capture and discrepancy resolution?

already_counted.description: Actual verification, capture and final reconciliation

incremental.description: Counter checks and offline exception review

approvals.approved_version: Exact service, stops, movement entries, exceptions and totals; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R75 gross25 minus6 upkeep gives net19. Range0-5 allows existing counters or costly offline reconciliation to absorb most arithmetic saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Less repeated lookup and tallying where complete current inputs exist.
reach: Coordinate source freshness and count definitions with transport control
role.ambitious_version: An attendant with reliable information and counts while remaining responsible for customer assistance.
